objective.value: Improve N-acetyl-D-neuraminic acid (NeuAc) production in Escherichia coli from glucose as sole carbon source by (1) optimizing amino sugar metabolism pathway kinetics via screening AGE and NeuB enzymes from different sources and their combinations, (2) optimizing expression intensity of the two key enzymes via RBS engineering, and (3) reserving the phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) pool by engineering the PEP catabolic pathway (knockout of ptsG, pykA, pykF, ppc, pck, gltA candidates).

hypothesis.value: NeuAc synthesis is bottlenecked by amino sugar metabolism (the GlcNAc-to-NeuAc steps catalyzed by AGE and NeuB are rate-limiting) and by unbalanced precursor PEP supply due to inherent glycolytic regulation; systematically optimizing enzyme kinetics/expression and metabolic flux distribution at the PEP node should holistically improve NeuAc production.
hypothesis.notes: Rate-limiting-step attribution for GlcNAc→NeuAc steps is cited by the authors to prior studies (refs 36, 37); PEP bottleneck inference in this study is triggered by observed GlcNAc/ManNAc accumulation.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (heterologous enzyme combination constructed in this study), Q2 pass (constructed here, though pB plasmid template derives from prior study ref 36 — the six combination plasmids were built in this work), Q3 pass (combination choice drove subsequent RBS and knockout decisions).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Replacing rate-limiting enzymes with natural high-activity orthologs and screening their combinations = rate-limiting enzyme identification and engineering.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Prior directed evolution could only improve enzymes within inherent characteristics; GlcNAc→NeuAc steps reported as rate-limiting (refs 36,37); existing titers far from cost-effective.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Choice of orthologs based on reported high enzymatic activities (literature-reported measured kinetics); outcomes measured by fermentation titers in this study.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Enzymes explicitly 'chosen because they have reported high enzymatic activities' (refs 28, 41–43) — selection justified by literature-reported properties rather than new mechanistic analysis in this paper.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When the two terminal steps of an amino-sugar-to-NeuAc pathway are rate-limiting in an E. coli production system, apply screening of natural high-activity AGE and NeuB orthologs and their source combinations, because orthologs differ in substrate affinity and temperature adaptation which jointly determine pathway flux.
alternatives_considered: Directed evolution of AGE via high-threshold riboswitch (used previously, ref 37) — set aside because it can only improve inherent enzyme characteristics

experiments.purpose: Improve expression intensity of all NeuAc pathway genes
experiments.intervention: Vectors of different copy numbers (p15a-cagg, pCDF-cagg, pUC-cagg) and strong PT7 promoter constructs (pET-cagg, pET-acgg, p15a-T7p-cam)
experiments.conditions: Fermentation with inducer addition (standard MTB/IPTG conditions inferred)
experiments.outcome: Growth severely inhibited after induction; NeuAc production significantly decreased (data not shown); strategy abandoned

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (promoter/copy-number engineering action), Q2 pass (constructed in this study), Q3 pass (negative result redirected strategy toward RBS fine-tuning).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Attempted expression-level adjustment of pathway genes (copy number and strong promoter) = expression balancing.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: AGE and NeuB shown critical to NeuAc production; authors hypothesized enhancing expression intensity could further increase production.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Outcome (growth inhibition, decreased production) was experimentally observed, though data not shown.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper states the conclusion ('strong expression caused metabolism to become seriously uncoordinated') as a post-result interpretation without mechanistic measurement; no explicit a priori mechanistic reason given for choosing PT7 beyond generic 'strong promoter'.

experiments.purpose: Fine-tune expression intensity of AGE_a and NeuB_c to efficiently metabolize accumulated GlcNAc
experiments.intervention: RBS substitution upstream of AGE_a in pBac (ARBS1–4, predicted initiation strengths 32,837–146,797 vs ARBS0 10,146) then NeuB_c in pBac2 (NRBS1–4, 12,109–109,625 vs NRBS0 6,993), designed with RBS Calculator 2.0; reverse PCR with RBS-containing primers
experiments.conditions: Batch fermentation, 20 g/L glucose, 30 °C, 36 h; fed fermentation of DN5/pBacR
experiments.control: Original RBS strains (ARBS0 / NRBS0) (baseline, inferred role)
experiments.readout: NeuAc titer, glucose consumption, GlcNAc/ManNAc accumulation
experiments.analysis: Titer vs predicted RBS intensity; selected ARBS2 (3.2 g/L) and NRBS3 (3.7 g/L)
experiments.outcome: pBacR (ARBS2+NRBS3); fed fermentation 7.1 g/L NeuAc at 96 h; 12.6 g/L GlcNAc + 2.5 g/L ManNAc accumulated, indicating amino sugar supply sufficient and bottleneck shifting to PEP supply

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (RBS engineering performed), Q2 pass (this study), Q3 pass (established pBacR chassis for subsequent PEP engineering; revealed next bottleneck).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Modulating translation initiation strength of the two key enzymes to balance pathway expression = expression balancing.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: GlcNAc accumulation remained very high during fermentation, indicating downstream conversion capacity insufficient; strong PT7 expression caused metabolic discoordination, so moderate tunable tuning was needed.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: RBS selection based on RBS Calculator 2.0 predicted translation initiation intensities — predictive tool output; predictions were then confirmed by fermentation, but the design rationale itself rests on prediction (需实测确认, which the authors did perform).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives an explicit mechanistic rationale: high GlcNAc accumulation means AGE/NeuB throughput limits flux, so raising their translation intensity should drain GlcNAc toward NeuAc; non-monotonic response at highest RBS is mechanistically attributed (with hedging 'may') to low NeuB_c solubility.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an intermediate (GlcNAc) accumulates in an E. coli NeuAc production system, apply moderate RBS-strength tuning of the downstream enzymes (AGE/NeuB) rather than maximal-strength promoters, because balanced translation increase raises pathway throughput while avoiding metabolic burden or solubility limits of heterologous enzymes.
alternatives_considered: Strong PT7 promoter / high-copy vectors — abandoned due to severe growth inhibition

experiments.purpose: Reserve PEP pool for NeuAc synthesis by blocking PEP consumption pathways
experiments.intervention: Knockout of six PEP-node genes (ptsG, pykA, pykF, ppc, pck, gltA) individually from DN5 via pTKRed recombineering; second round: gltA or ptsG knocked out from DN11; pykF double-knockout deliberately not attempted
experiments.conditions: Fed fermentation in shake flasks, 30 °C, 220 rpm, pH ~7.0 (30% NH4OH), sampling 6/12 h, stopped at 120 h
experiments.replicates: Three independent experiments; Figure 5D representative curve RSD < 10%
experiments.readout: NeuAc, GlcNAc, ManNAc titers; OD600; growth phenotype in LB vs TB
experiments.analysis: Titer comparison across knockout strains; growth defect interpretation
experiments.outcome: ΔpykA best single knockout (9.9 g/L, strain DN11); Δppc severe growth defect; Δpck reduced NeuAc; DN11ΔgltA fell to 5.6 g/L; DN11ΔptsG = DN12 reached 16.7 g/L — highest reported NeuAc production from glucose as sole carbon source

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 pass (genome knockouts performed), Q2 pass (this study), Q3 pass (results selected DN11 and DN12 and defined which PEP routes are safely blockable).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Blocking competing PEP consumption routes to increase precursor PEP availability for NeuB reaction = precursor and reducing-power supply (precursor supply).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: DN5/pBacR fed fermentation accumulated 12.6 g/L GlcNAc and 2.5 g/L ManNAc, indicating amino sugar supply sufficient and the bottleneck had shifted to PEP supply.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Target selection based on literature-reported stoichiometric distribution of PEP consumption (ref 44: PTS ~50%, ppc 16.2%, pyruvate kinase 14.5%, aromatics 3.3%) — chemical-stoichiometric knowledge; outcomes experimentally measured.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives explicit mechanism: ptsG knockout reroutes glucose transport from PEP-consuming PTS to ATP-consuming transport, sparing PEP; pykA knockout reduces flux toward pyruvate kinase; gltA double-knockout harms energy supply; pck catalyzes oxaloacetate→PEP direction so its removal lowers PEP supply. These are mechanistic (though partly hedged with 'may') explanations tied to pathway topology.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When PEP-dependent product synthesis is bottlenecked by PEP supply in an E. coli glucose-fermentation system, apply stepwise deletion of major PEP-consuming nodes (pyruvate kinase pykA, then PTS component ptsG) while preserving anaplerosis and at least one pyruvate-kinase route, because PTS and pyruvate kinase consume the largest PEP shares, but complete glycolytic or TCA blockage (pykA+pykF, gltA on ΔpykA) collapses precursor/energy supply.
alternatives_considered: pykF knockout on DN11 background — not tried because pykA+pykF would fully block glycolysis and deprive acetyl-CoA supply for GNA1
ppc knockout — severe growth reduction (oxaloacetate replenishment blocked)
gltA knockout on DN11 — NeuAc fell to 5.6 g/L (energy shortage)
'some other PEP consumption routes were adopted for engineering but all ended in failure' (unspecified)
